title: [Mouse Without Borders] Impossible to run without elevated privileges, Impossible to change layout
author: HattDroid
summary: Mouse Without Borders blocks layout drag-and-drop because the running Settings process is elevated; the report does not yet show whether PowerToys still launches elevated after a complete normal restart.

status.label: Needs elevation-state evidence
status.detail: The drag restriction is intentional for elevated WinUI, but the remaining question is why PowerToys appears to stay elevated after the admin toggle is disabled.

next_action.label: Request focused elevation diagnostics
next_action.reason: Confirm the post-restart process elevation state and collect a fresh archive only if PowerToys still starts elevated.

judgment.rationale: This is not yet proven to be a 0.101 regression. The visible message matches an intentional elevated-process safeguard, while the unresolved part is whether PowerToys can restart unelevated after the setting is disabled.
evidence: The issue reports PowerToys 0.101.2362 installed with WinGet and quotes the Mouse Without Borders elevated-process drag-and-drop warning.
The reporter says disabling the Run as administrator toggle did not restore layout editing.
MouseWithoutBordersViewModel.cs assigns CanDragDrop = !IsElevated, and MouseWithoutBordersPage.xaml binds drag/drop to that value because elevated WinUI drag can crash.
There are no assignees, linked fixes, or duplicate issues in the current timeline.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for the elevation state after a full tray exit/restart and request /bugreport only if PowerToys still starts elevated.

issue_context.summary: The layout editor remains locked behind an elevated-process warning after the reporter turns off the administrator setting.
known_information: Mouse Without Borders displays the explicit message that drag-and-drop is not possible while PowerToys is elevated.
The reporter states that the Run as administrator toggle was turned off.
No diagnostic archive, assignee, duplicate, or linked fix is present.
inferences: The current process may still have elevated rights because changing the setting cannot de-elevate an already-running process.
If a clean restart remains elevated, startup configuration, compatibility settings, service mode, or policy may be forcing elevation.
issue_context.analysis: The repository evidence explains why dragging is disabled while elevated, but it does not explain whether this reporter is stuck elevated after a clean restart. That distinction determines whether the response is usage guidance or an elevation/startup bug investigation.
initial_investigation: src/settings-ui/Settings.UI/ViewModels/MouseWithoutBordersViewModel.cs sets each device tile CanDragDrop to false when GeneralSettingsConfig.IsElevated is true.
src/settings-ui/Settings.UI/SettingsXAML/Views/MouseWithoutBordersPage.xaml binds AllowDrop and CanDrag to CanDragDrop and documents the WinUI elevated-drag crash workaround.
Targeted duplicate search found only this issue for Mouse Without Borders elevated layout editing.

information_gaps.how_to_collect: Exit PowerToys from the tray, verify no PowerToys processes remain in Task Manager, restart normally, and report whether Task Manager shows PowerToys as elevated.

information_gaps.information: A fresh diagnostic archive if PowerToys still starts elevated after that clean restart.

comment.body: Thanks for the clear PowerToys 0.101.2362 report and exact Mouse Without Borders warning. The layout editor intentionally disables WinUI drag-and-drop while the running PowerToys process is elevated, and turning off the setting does not lower an already-running process. Please fully exit PowerToys from the tray, confirm in Task Manager that no PowerToys processes remain, restart normally with `Run as administrator` disabled, and tell us whether Task Manager still shows PowerToys as elevated. If it still starts elevated, reproduce the locked layout once and then add a comment containing `/bugreport` immediately so the generated ZIP captures that startup state; please also mention any executable compatibility setting or organizational policy that forces PowerToys to run as administrator.
